paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，您有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“人们越来越意识到当今世界数字素养和技能的重要性。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。您应该写至少 150 个字，但不能超过

paragraphs.sourceText: than 200 words. (You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.)
paragraphs.translationZh: 超过200字。 （您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。）

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《太阳也是一颗星星》是一个关于爱情、浪漫、命运和命运的真正可爱的故事。

paragraphs.sourceText: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living 26 in America, not by choice exactly. Her parents brought her over and created the situation she 27 to be out of.
paragraphs.translationZh: 娜塔莎是牙买加出生的移民，非法居住在美国，这并不是她的选择。她的父母把她带了过来，并创造了她努力摆脱的局面。

paragraphs.sourceText: Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha 28 through scientific reasoning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 丹尼尔是出生于美国的韩国移民。他相信真爱、命运，以及娜塔莎通过科学推理驳斥的所有其他废话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Daniel and Natasha meet by 29 on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be 30 . She doesn’t tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 丹尼尔和娜塔莎在她将被驱逐出境的那天在纽约街头巧合。她没有告诉他这一点，但确实允许他在一天中试图让她爱上他的同时陪伴她。

paragraphs.sourceText: Natasha is me. I found her so similar to myself. She’s scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always 31 . Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I 32 Daniel seeing that too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 娜塔莎就是我。我发现她和我很相似。她有科学头脑，务实，有点愤世嫉俗，并且总是持怀疑态度。她通过科学视角对宇宙的痴迷具有感染力，我也喜欢丹尼尔看到这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even 33 Natasha’s tough outer shell. By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 丹尼尔迷人而热情，他的言辞甚至能打破娜塔莎坚韧的外壳。读完这本书后，我爱上了他们两个。

paragraphs.sourceText: I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. I got 34 in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn’t wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我曾经觉得浪漫故事总是廉价或可笑的。我想现在我可以看到逃避纯粹乐观故事的价值。我在《太阳也是一颗星星》中迷失了方向，并在一个周末的时间里从头到尾看完了它。我迫不及待地想要得到一个幸福的结局。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s nice every once in a while to give in to magic. It doesn’t have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. That 35 that causes them to react and spark when they’re near each other.
paragraphs.translationZh: 偶尔屈服于魔法真是太好了。它不一定是一本带有实际咒语的硬奇幻小说，它可以是两个拥有特殊东西的人之间发现的魔法。当它们彼此靠近时，这种化学反应会导致它们发生反应并产生火花。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: These are the habits to avoid if you want to make a behavior change
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你想改变行为，这些是要避免的习惯

paragraphs.sourceText: A) According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. Once we’ve successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 根据最近的研究，行为改变涉及大脑的物理变化。在过去的十年中，研究人员表明，当谈到将一种新行为变成根深蒂固的习惯的持续时间时，没有一个简单的答案。即使对于我们当中最有生产力、最自律的人来说，要消除一些已经成为我们的自然组成部分的东西也不是一朝一夕的努力就能做到的。一旦我们成功地做出了改变，我们就必须对我们的生活进行其他调整，以确保我们继续维持它，这本身通常是一个完全不同的挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. When there isn’t the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 从本质上讲，如果不引入某种系统，就很难成功地改变和维持某种行为。如果没有适当的框架，我们来之不易的进步就更有可能脱轨。为了确保成功改变和维持行为，我们应该远离一些有害的习惯。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. Perhaps you didn’t want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p.m. Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 第一个要避免的是依靠意志力。想想你上次发誓要抵制诱惑是什么时候。也许您不想每 15 分钟查看一次手机，或者您决定不在下午 3 点去拿一块巧克力。想象一下，当你触手可及的时候不看一眼手机，或者当你下午精神萎靡时不走到自动售货机那一定有多困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can’t change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. The old military saying “You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training” also applies to behavior change. The idea is simple — you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）关于我们的意志力是有限还是无限的研究还没有定论，但专家们普遍认为，如果你仅依靠意志力，你就无法改变和维持一个习惯。古老的军事格言“你永远不会适应这种情况，你只会下降到训练的水平”也适用于行为改变。这个想法很简单——你重复某件事很多次，它就会变得自动。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Think about what else you can change about your surrounding that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. This is called your “cue.” Basically, it’s a trigger to perform that particular habit. If you don’t want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p.m., have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. When 3 p.m. comes around, that’s your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 想想你还可以改变周围的环境，让你更容易每天进行这种改变。这就是所谓的“提示”。基本上，它是执行该特定习惯的触发器。如果您不想在下午 3 点喝点甜食，可以在办公桌上准备一盒花草茶。下午 3 点的时候出现这种情况时，提示您给自己倒一杯热水并喝茶，而不是走到自动售货机那里。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. Sometimes, it’s not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. However, this habit-learning system isn’t so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. That’s why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 第二个要避免的目标是关注消极目标。有时候，让你失望的不是你的过程，而是你首先想要改变的习惯。首先，与到达指定时间时用巧克力代替花草茶相比，不吃巧克力来缓解下午的低迷状态是一个更难的目标。你的大脑想要找到过去成功的例程，并允许你在未来再次重复这些动作，而无需明确地思考它们。然而，当学习不做某事时，这种习惯学习系统就不那么有效了。这就是为什么与其放弃某些东西，不如考虑引入一些东西来代替它。专注于你将要采取的行动，这些行动最终会与你想要停止的行为发生冲突。当你的注意力集中在做新事物上时，你的习惯系统就有机会发挥作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. Because we are creatures of habit, it’s natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that’s not always the case. Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 第三个要避免的就是在不同的情况下使用相同的策略。因为我们是习惯的生物，所以很自然地认为，当我们确实设法采取并维持一种理想的行为时，当我们想要改变另一种行为时，同样的策略也会起作用。但情况并非总是如此。有时，让你改变一种行为的系统可能不适用于另一种行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 有时，我们在做决定时习惯于依靠自己的直觉。这在某些情况下对我们很有帮助，但在其他情况下可能会阻碍我们，特别是当我们需要考虑指标和数据，而不是让我们的直觉凌驾于一切时。例如，如果您想在早上第一件事停止检查电子邮件，您可能会决定用其他活动来代替。但如果你想停止沉迷于电子游戏，仅仅决定去跑步可能并不那么有效。您可能需要引入另一种强化措施，例如与朋友见面并一起预订健身课程。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you found yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. Or you prepared meals on Sunday and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn’t mean you can’t start afresh the next day.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 第四个要避免的就是不原谅自己的失误。当然，即使是最周密的计划有时也会失败。您可能已经坚持了五天没有屏幕的夜间例行公事，然后一个大项目落在您的办公桌上，您发现自己在睡觉前躺在床上，拿着笔记本电脑。或者你周日准备了饭菜，并坚持在家吃健康的晚餐，但到了周五，你发现自己太累了，选择了点油腻的外卖。生活会发生，即使你的行为改变很小，每一天都可能变得相当不灵活，在某些时候你的运气可能会耗尽，即使只是一天。你身上的完美主义者可能会尖叫着完全放弃你的目标，但试着从更大的角度来看待它。仅仅因为您可能暂时偏离了方向，并不意味着您无法在第二天重新开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. There’s a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don’t take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. Your brain responds to rewards. The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cued, and at the end, when it’s rewarded. Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Rather than focusing on how far you’ve gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you’ve made. It doesn’t have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 最后要避免的一点是低估小进步。许多完美主义者在试图改变行为时往往会陷入一种习惯。他们过于关注大目标，而没有花时间庆祝他们在此过程中取得的小进步。你的大脑会对奖励做出反应。基底神经节是与我们的习惯表现相关的大脑区域，在行为开始时（当习惯受到暗示时）和结束时（当习惯得到奖励时）最活跃。假设您的目标是每周跑 3 次 5 英里，而本周您在周一、周三和周五跑了一英里。不要关注你已经实现了多少目标，而是考虑如何奖励自己所取得的进步。它不必很大或很昂贵；它可以像跑步后制作您最喜欢的果汁一样简单。无论您的奖励是什么，它都不能只是让您继续前进的活动本身。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. But they won’t. Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! Which is why it’s so hard to maintain new behaviors.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 发起新的行为通常看起来是改变过程中最困难的部分。然而，人们常常未能为维护它做好充分的准备。造成这种情况的原因之一是我们错误地认为我们用于发起变革的策略将同样有效地帮助我们继续变革。但他们不会。改变根深蒂固的习惯需要改变我们对这种深深渗透到我们生活中的习惯的信念，不断地体现出智慧需要我们保持积极的态度。如果我们情绪低落，改变行为的智慧似乎就会消失，我们就会回到多吃少运动的状态。因此，保持新行为的关键是快乐！这就是为什么保持新行为如此困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. No one was born with habits. They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. The question is: how badly do you really want to change?
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 请记住，克服阻碍我们实施新改变的行为惯性，例如健康饮食或锻炼，从长远来看可以使我们受益，并可以改善我们的身心健康。没有人一出生就有习惯。它们都是有学问的，因此也都可以被忘却。问题是：你到底有多想改变？

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. There is general consensus among experts that willpower alone cannot guarantee one’s success in changing and maintaining a habit.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 专家们普遍认为，单靠意志力并不能保证一个人成功改变和保持习惯。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. One need not abandon their goals completely just because they missed their target temporarily; they can start anew.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 一个人不必因为暂时没有达到目标而完全放弃目标；他们可以重新开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Research shows it is quite another challenge to maintain a behavioral change after you have initiated it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 研究表明，在开始行为改变后保持行为改变是另一项挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. It is wrong to assume the strategies we use to start a change of behavior will work equally well in helping maintain it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 假设我们用来开始改变行为的策略在帮助维持行为方面同样有效，这是错误的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Sometimes, it may not be successful to simply substitute one activity with another to effect a change of habit; you may need extra reinforcement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 有时，简单地用一项活动替代另一项活动来改变习惯可能并不成功；你可能需要额外的强化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. One should introduce something new to replace an old habit instead of simply kicking it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一个人应该引入一些新的东西来取代旧的习惯，而不是简单地改掉它。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Perfectionists focus too much on their big target and neglect celebrating the small gains they make in the process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 完美主义者过于关注他们的大目标，而忽视庆祝他们在这个过程中取得的小成就。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. It is of great benefit to us in the long term to conquer the inertia that stops us from making behavioral changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 从长远来看，克服阻止我们做出行为改变的惯性对我们大有裨益。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The strategy that successfully changed one of your behaviors may not work for some other behavior of yours.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 成功改变你的一种行为的策略可能不适用于你的其他一些行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Without a happy mood, it seems that our wisdom to adopt a different behavior vanishes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 没有愉快的心情，我们采取不同行为的智慧似乎就消失了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The “American Dream” promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
paragraphs.translationZh: “美国梦”承诺，在机遇之地，任何个人都可以通过努力工作和雄心壮志攀登经济阶梯并走向繁荣。然而，今天的美国年轻人正在努力挣得比他们的父辈在同龄时更多的钱，而且美国的向上流动性实际上与其他工业化国家相比并不理想。

paragraphs.sourceText: So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，为什么美国梦的理念能够持续存在呢？ 《美国政治学杂志》上的一项新研究发现了一个被忽视的因素：真人秀的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a “rags-to-riches” storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts — which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans — get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.
paragraphs.translationZh: 范德比尔特大学的 Eunji Kim 指出，过去 20 年来，真人秀节目已经在美国电视界占据主导地位。其中绝大多数都有一个“白手起家”的故事情节：它们的主角是普通美国人，他们努力工作以取得巨大的经济成功。虽然这些节目通常是收视率最高的节目之一，但新闻广播——更现实地描述了数百万美国人面临的经济困难——所占的收视比例要小得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous (无处不在的) on TV — but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim’s team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn’t have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.
paragraphs.translationZh: 白手起家的故事在电视上随处可见——但是观看这些节目真的能让人们相信经济流动是很容易实现的吗？为了找到答案，Kim 的团队让参与者观看了一段 5 分钟的真人秀片段，讲述了白手起家的故事情节。对照组参与者观看了真人秀节目的剪辑，该节目没有白手起家的故事。观看节目后，参与者评估了他们对与美国梦有关的四项陈述的同意程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: The results showed that those who’d watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 结果表明，那些看过白手起家视频的人确实对美国梦抱有更大的信念。有趣的是，当参与者按党派关系分开时，这种效应在共和党人中显着，而在民主党人中则不然，这表明这些电视节目中隐含的信息可能会影响人们现有的社会经济信仰。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.
paragraphs.translationZh: Kim 还对 3000 名美国居民进行了一项调查。他们还评估了他们认为生活中的成功与各种内部因素（例如野心）和外部因素（例如家庭财富）相关的程度。最后，他们阅读了一份电视节目列表并指出了他们经常观看的节目。

paragraphs.sourceText: Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经常观看白手起家节目的参与者比那些从未观看过此类节目的参与者对美国梦有更强烈的信念。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kim concludes that “rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility”. And here’s the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 金的结论是，“白手起家的娱乐媒体是促进和延续向上流动信念的重要文化力量”。问题是：如果人们错误地认为，个人只需要努力工作就能过上更好的生活，那么他们可能不太支持真正消除不平等的政策。

paragraphs.sourceText: “In this era of choice, entertainment media are what captures hearts and minds,” Kim writes. “Its political consequences are anything but trivial”.
paragraphs.translationZh: “在这个选择的时代，娱乐媒体才是俘获人心的东西，”金写道。 “其政治后果绝非微不足道”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When someone asks us “what do you do?” we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当有人问我们“你是做什么的？”我们几乎总是以我们的职业来回答。对于我们许多人来说，工作不仅仅是一份工作。这是我们身份的决定性方面。对于我们许多人来说，我们可以通过工作来定义自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Without my job I don’t know who I am,” is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: “没有工作，我就不知道自己是谁”，这句话在我的办公椅上不止一次说过。事实上，这可能是我与失去或被迫换工作的客户合作的最具挑战性的方面之一。这种损失引发的身份危机比失去工作本身还要严重得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today’s volatile and ever-shifting job market.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是，我们的身份比我们乍一看要复杂得多。如果我们花时间反思，我们可能会认识到，除了我们的工作外，我们还可以将自己视为朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父母、运动队或宗教团体的成员。我们可能会认识到，我们在这些角色和关系中的感受和行为与在工作中的不同。被动的女儿在工作中成为自信的领导者。此外，我们在工作中的身份并不是一成不变的。它们随着时间的推移而改变。我本人曾当过店员、女服务员、学生、毕业生和临床心理学家。在每个阶段，我适应和发展职业身份的能力对我的幸福至关重要。虽然我们希望在某种程度上消除生活中的不确定性，但我们必须管理不确定性，尤其是在当今动荡且不断变化的就业市场中。

paragraphs.sourceText: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves “I’m good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through” it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们如何看待自己是我们身份问题的核心。当我们告诉自己“我擅长启动项目，但不太擅长完成项目”时，它可以成为我们信念体系的一部分。但如果你有过被迫换工作的不幸经历，你就需要审视这些信念，看看它们在现实中的根基如何。您将需要问自己这些信念有多大帮助并考虑个人改变。我们可以通过实验、实践和有意识的自律随时改变我们的信念、行为和情感体验。在职业发展可能引导我们进入新领域的时代，挑战自我意识并探索是否可以通过改变对自己的信念来创造新的身份体验以扩大职业选择变得更加重要。最终，是你自己决定了你是谁。如果你顺其自然的话，你就是你的工作。
